result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers turn the switch into an accessible button with role="switch" and aria-checked, add focus rings, and keep the /api/prefs payload. Answer A has a hidden bug: it declares `var status` at global scope, which collides with the legacy `window.status` string property, so its Saved and error messages never appear. Answer B uses `const`, which avoids that collision, so its feedback works, and it also styles the Save button, although it keeps the faint #ccc off track. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers make the switch a real button with role=switch, aria-checked and a proper accessible name, add visible focus rings, keep the /api/prefs payload, and add save feedback. B's save handling is a little stronger: it shows the error in red, says plainly that the choice is kept and how to retry, and fixes the faint off-state contrast. A responds more directly to the 'looks rough' complaint by styling the Save button, setting fonts and spacing, and adding a reduced-motion-safe transition, while B leaves Save as a default browser button.

passes.notes: Both answers turn the switch into an accessible button with role="switch" and aria-checked, add focus rings, and keep the /api/prefs payload. Answer A has a hidden bug: it declares `var status` at global scope, which collides with the legacy `window.status` string property, so its Saved and error messages never appear. Answer B uses `const`, which avoids that collision, so its feedback works, and it also styles the Save button, although it keeps the faint #ccc off track.
